gloss: womb; compassion, tender love; have compassion
summary: The root's ground is the womb, רֶחֶם, and from it comes the tender feeling of one who bore a child: a mother's compassion for “the son of her womb” (Isa 49:15), whose inward parts “grew warm” for her son (1Ki 3:26). The plural רַחֲמִים is that compassion, above all Yahweh's; the piel רִחַם is to have compassion, as a father on his children (Psa 103:13), most often of Yahweh turning back to Israel after wrath and restoring them to their land; the adjective רַחוּם “compassionate” is said only of God, in the words he proclaimed of his own name (Exo 34:6). The one qal, “I love you, Yahweh” (Psa 18:2), matches the Aramaic and the Peshitta's Syriac, where the verb is the ordinary word for love. Arabic raḥim “womb” and raḥima “have mercy”, and Akkadian rēmu “womb; mercy”, join the same two sides; the unclean bird רָחָם is a second older root, Arabic raḫam “vulture”.

words.gloss: womb; (from the womb) from birth; (once) a girl
words.summary: About thirty times in the singular, the womb that Yahweh closes and opens and in which he forms a man; with מִן it is “from birth”. It is feminine in Jer 20:17 (וְרַחְמָהּ הֲרַת), and in Jdg 5:30 it names a captive girl. The plural רַחֲמִים is filed as its own word below.

senses.definition: The womb of a woman or a beast, where a child is conceived and formed; Yahweh closes it and opens it. The firstborn is “the opener of the womb”.

evidence.note: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated “and opened her רַחְמָהּ, and Rachel was barren”.
God remembered Rachel “and opened her womb”.
Yahweh “had completely closed every רֶחֶם of the house of Abimelech”.
“Yahweh had shut her womb.”
“Did not he who made me in the belly (בֶּטֶן) make him, and one fashion us in the womb?”
“That my mother might have been my grave, and her womb pregnant for ever.”
“Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.”
“Blessings of the breasts and of the womb.”
“The grave, and the barren womb” among the things never satisfied.
“Set apart to me every firstborn, the opener of every womb (פֶּטֶר כָּל־רֶחֶם) among the sons of Israel, of man and of beast.”
Israel “caused every opener of the womb to pass through” the fire.
Of the sea, “when it burst out, it came forth from the womb”.
“From the womb of the dawn”: figurative.
Quoting Exo 13:2, 12 of Jesus: “every male that opens the womb (μήτραν) shall be called holy to the Lord”.

senses.definition: With מִן, and in parallel with מִבֶּטֶן: from the moment of birth, from the beginning of a man's life.

evidence.note: “On you I was cast מֵרָחֶם; from my mother's belly you are my God.”
“The wicked are estranged from the womb; they go astray from the belly, speaking lies.”
“Carried from the belly, borne from the womb.”
“Before you came out of the womb I set you apart.”
“Why did I not die from the womb?”
“Like the dead, whose flesh is half eaten when he comes out of his mother's womb.”
Of the wicked man: “the womb forgets him; the worm feeds sweetly on him.”

senses.definition: Once, of captive women counted as spoil: “a womb, two wombs” for each warrior.

evidence.note: Sisera's mother imagines the spoil: “רַחַם רַחֲמָתַיִם to the head of a man.”

evidence.locator: EXO 13:2 word 7, רֶחֶם → μήτραν; GEN 49:25 μήτρας; JER 1:5 μήτρας; PSA 22:11 μήτρας; μήτρα renders רֶחֶם ×14, κοιλία ×4

evidence.note: “Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”, quoting the law of Exo 13:2, 12 at Jesus' presentation.
“The deadness of Sarah's womb”, as Yahweh had closed and opened wombs in Genesis.

parallels.note: “Breasts”: womb and breasts together for bearing and nursing.

phrases.gloss: opener of the womb, the firstborn

words.gloss: compassion, tender mercies; the inward parts that yearn
words.summary: The plural of רֶחֶם, used always of feeling: the inward parts that grow warm for a brother or a son, and so compassion. Most often it is Yahweh's, “great” and “many”, joined with חֶסֶד; Yahweh also “gives” a man compassion before his captors or a ruler. The database files the same tokens under רֶחֶם too.

senses.gloss: the inward parts, stirred with feeling
senses.definition: The inward parts as the seat of tender feeling, which “grow warm” (נִכְמְרוּ) toward a brother or a child.

evidence.note: The true mother, “for her רַחֲמִים grew warm over her son”, says, “give her the living child, and by no means kill it”.
Joseph hurried out, “for his רַחֲמִים grew warm toward his brother, and he sought to weep”.
“The yearning of your bowels (מֵעֶיךָ) and your compassion toward me are restrained.”
“The righteous knows the soul of his beast, but the רַחֲמִים of the wicked are cruel.”

senses.definition: Yahweh's tender mercy toward his people and his works: great and many, from of old, not exhausted, the ground of forgiveness and of restoration.

evidence.note: “The covenant faithfulness of Yahweh: we are not consumed, for his compassions do not fail.”
“According to the multitude of your compassions, blot out my transgressions.”
“Remember your compassions, Yahweh, and your covenant faithfulnesses, for they are from of old.”
“Yahweh is good to all, and his compassions are over all his works.”
“For a small moment I forsook you, but with great compassions I will gather you.”
David: “Let us fall into the hand of Yahweh, for his compassions are many, and let me not fall into the hand of man.”
“To the Lord our God belong compassions and forgivenesses, for we have rebelled against him.”
“Not for our righteousnesses … but for your great compassions.”
“In your great compassions you did not forsake them in the wilderness.”
“Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he shut up his compassions in anger?”
“Who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with covenant faithfulness and compassions.”
“I will betroth you to me in righteousness and justice, in covenant faithfulness and compassions.”
“I have returned to Jerusalem with compassions; my house shall be built in it.”
“That Yahweh may turn from his burning anger and give you compassion, and have compassion on you.”
“I have taken away my peace from this people … the covenant faithfulness and the compassions.”
“The Father of compassions (οἰκτιρμῶν)”; the Peshitta has the same root, אַבָֿא דּרַחמֵא.
“By the compassions of God”; Peshitta בּרַחמַוה_י דַּאלָהָא.

senses.definition: Pity of one man toward another: given by God before captors or a ruler, commanded between brothers, and destroyed by the cruel.

evidence.note: “Give them compassion before their captors, that they may have compassion on them (וְרִחֲמוּם).”
“May God Almighty give you compassion before the man.”
“Give him compassion before this man.”
“God gave Daniel covenant faithfulness and compassion before the chief of the eunuchs.”
“Judge true judgment, and show covenant faithfulness and compassions each to his brother.”
Edom pursued his brother with the sword “and destroyed his compassions”.
Babylon “showed them no compassion”.

evidence.locator: PSA 51:3 word 5, רַחֲמֶיךָ → οἰκτιρμῶν; PSA 25:6; ISA 63:15; 1KI 8:50 οἰκτιρμούς; οἰκτιρμός renders רַחֲמִים ×18, ἔλεος ×6

evidence.note: “By the compassions of God”: the Peshitta has רַחמֵא.
“The Father of compassions.”
“Put on bowels of compassion (σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ).”
“Died without compassions”; Peshitta דּלָא רַחמִין.

evidence.locator: s.v. σπλάγχνον
evidence.note: Plural σπλάγχνα in the New Testament, equated with Hebrew רַחֲמִים.
“Through the tender compassions (σπλάγχνα ἐλέους) of our God, by which the dayspring from on high has visited us”; the Peshitta has בּרַחמֵא.
“In the bowels of Jesus Christ”; Peshitta בּרַחמַוה_י.
“Shuts up his bowels from him”; Peshitta רַחמַוה_י.

opposites.note: “Cruel”: what the compassion of the wicked is.

phrases.gloss: his inward parts grew warm, he was deeply moved

words.gloss: (qal) love; (piel) have compassion; (pual) be shown compassion
words.summary: About forty-five times, almost all piel: to have compassion, as a mother on the son of her womb (Isa 49:15) and a father on his children (Psa 103:13). Its subject is nearly always Yahweh, and its partner חָנַן; with “not” it is the pitilessness of a conqueror. The one qal (Psa 18:2) is “love”, the verb's sense in Aramaic and Syriac. The brief's three tokens with no stem (Hos 1:6, 8; 2:25) are the name Lo-ruhamah, a pual form.

senses.definition: Once, David's love for Yahweh, his strength and deliverer.

evidence.note: “And he said, אֶרְחָמְךָ, Yahweh, my strength”; the parallel 2Sa 22:2 lacks the line.

senses.definition: To feel and show tender pity toward one in need or under judgment, as a parent toward a child; of Yahweh, to turn from wrath to restore, forgive and gather his people.

evidence.note: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, so as not to have compassion (מֵרַחֵם) on the son of her womb? Even these may forget, but I will not forget you.”
“As a father has compassion on his children, Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.”
“I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion (וְרִחַמְתִּי) on whom I will have compassion.”
Quoting Exo 33:19: οἰκτιρήσω; the Peshitta has the pael, אֵרַחֵמ.
“Yahweh your God will turn your captivity and have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples.”
“In a flood of wrath I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting covenant faithfulness I will have compassion on you.”
“In my wrath I struck you, but in my favour I have had compassion on you.”
“In wrath remember compassion (רַחֵם).”
“Is Ephraim my dear son? … my inward parts (מֵעַי) yearn for him; I will surely have compassion on him.”
“Let the wicked forsake his way … and return to Yahweh, and he will have compassion on him.”
“He will again have compassion on us; he will subdue our iniquities.”
“Though he causes grief, he will have compassion according to the multitude of his covenant faithfulnesses.”
“Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.”
“He who has compassion on them (מְרַחֲמָם) will lead them, by springs of water he will guide them.”
“My covenant of peace shall not be removed, says Yahweh who has compassion on you.”
“I will have compassion on the house of Judah and save them by Yahweh their God.”
“How long will you not have compassion on Jerusalem … these seventy years?”
“You will arise and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to be gracious to her.”
“Yahweh is gracious and righteous; our God has compassion (מְרַחֵם).”
Of captors: “that they may have compassion on them”.

senses.definition: Negated: to show no pity in judgment or war, beside “not spare” and “not pity”; of Yahweh's withdrawn compassion and of cruel conquerors.

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar “will not pity them (לֹא־יָחוּס), and will not spare (לֹא יַחְמֹל), and will not have compassion (לֹא יְרַחֵם)”.
The Medes “will have no compassion on the fruit of the belly; their eye will not pity sons”.
“They are cruel (אַכְזָרִי) and have no compassion.”
“It is a people of no understanding; therefore he who made them will not have compassion on them.”
“I will no more have compassion on the house of Israel.”

senses.definition: To receive compassion: the fatherless from Yahweh, the one who confesses his sin; in Hosea the name of the daughter “not shown compassion” and its reversal.

evidence.note: “In you the fatherless is shown compassion (יְרֻחַם).”
“He who covers his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will be shown compassion.”
“Say to your sisters, Ruhamah”: “shown compassion”, the reversal of Lo-ruhamah.
לֹא רֻחָמָה “not shown compassion”, the daughter's name.
“Who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy”, from Hos 2:25; the Peshitta has רַחמֵא.
Quoting Hos 2:25: “her who was not beloved, beloved”; the Peshitta has the ethpeel אֵתֿרַחמַתֿ.

evidence.locator: DEU 30:3 word 6, רִחֲמְךָ → ἐλεήσει; ISA 54:8 ἐλεήσω; JER 31:20 ἐλεῶν, ἐλεήσω; HOS 1:6 ἐλεῆσαι; HOS 2:25 ἐλεήσω; ἐλεέω renders רָחַם about ×20

evidence.note: “Who had not obtained mercy (οὐκ ἠλεημένοι), but now have obtained mercy”, from Hosea's Lo-ruhamah.
“He has mercy on whom he will”; the Peshitta has מרַחֵמ.

evidence.note: Quoting Exo 33:19: “I will have compassion (οἰκτειρήσω) on whom I have compassion.”

evidence.locator: PSA 18:2 word 2, אֶרְחָמְךָ → ἀγαπήσω; PRO 28:13 יְרֻחָם → ἀγαπηθήσεται; ἀγαπάω renders רָחַם ×4

evidence.note: Quoting Hos 2:25: “her who was not beloved (ἠγαπημένην), beloved”.

parallels.note: “Pity, spare (with the eye)”, and חָמַל “spare”, beside it in the negative.

opposites.note: “Wrath”: compassion follows the wrath of judgment.

as a father has compassion on his children

words.summary: Thirteen times, every one of God, nearly always with חַנּוּן “gracious”, in the words Yahweh proclaimed of his own name (Exo 34:6) and their echoes; Psa 112:4 says it of the upright man who is like him.

senses.definition: Full of compassion: Yahweh's character, proclaimed with his name and pleaded by those who return to him.

evidence.note: “Yahweh, Yahweh, a God compassionate and gracious, long of anger and abounding in covenant faithfulness and truth.”
“Yahweh your God is a compassionate God; he will not forsake you nor destroy you nor forget the covenant of your fathers.”
“But he, being compassionate, covered iniquity and did not destroy … for he remembered that they were flesh” (v. 39).
“Return to Yahweh your God, for he is gracious and compassionate … and relents of evil.”
Jonah's complaint: “I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God”, toward Nineveh.
Of the upright: “gracious and compassionate and righteous”.
“The Lord is very compassionate (πολύσπλαγχνος) and merciful (οἰκτίρμων)”; the Peshitta has מרַחמָנ.

evidence.locator: EXO 34:6 word 9, רַחוּם → οἰκτίρμων; DEU 4:31; JOL 2:13; PSA 86:15; οἰκτίρμων renders רַחוּם ×12

evidence.note: “The Lord is very compassionate and merciful”, the words of Exo 34:6.
“Be compassionate, as your Father also is compassionate”; Peshitta מרַחמָנֵא.

parallels.note: “Gracious”: its partner in nearly every use.

phrases.phrase: אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד
phrases.gloss: a God compassionate and gracious, long of anger and abounding in covenant faithfulness

words.summary: Once, in the plural feminine: mothers, by nature the most compassionate, driven by the siege to boil their own children.

senses.definition: Full of compassion, of mothers; the horror of the siege is that such women ate their children.

evidence.note: “The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.”

words.summary: Twice, in the lists of unclean birds (רָחָם, and רָחָמָה in Deuteronomy). Arabic raḫam, the white Egyptian vulture, shows ḫ behind ח, so the bird is a second older root in this spelling, not the root of the womb and compassion (ḥ). The verses say only that it is unclean.

senses.definition: A bird not to be eaten, listed with the pelican and the cormorant; by the Arabic, the Egyptian vulture.

evidence.note: “And the owl, and the pelican, and the רָחָם.”
“And the pelican, and the רָחָמָה, and the cormorant.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once: the plural, as the Hebrew רַחֲמִים.

senses.definition: The compassion of the God of heaven, sought in prayer.

evidence.note: Daniel told his companions “to seek compassion (רַחֲמִין) from the God of heaven concerning this secret, that Daniel and his companions should not perish”.

words.gloss: (peal) love; (pael) have mercy; (ethpaal) have compassion; (ethpeel) be loved
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܪܚܡ, its common verb for “love” (ἀγαπάω, φιλέω), and in the derived stems for “have mercy, have compassion” (ἐλεέω, σπλαγχνίζομαι): the Hebrew's qal and piel side by side.

senses.definition: To love: God, one's neighbour, Jesus; for the Hebrew אָהַב in the commandments quoted.

evidence.note: “You shall love (דּתֵֿרחַמ) the Lord your God with all your heart”, quoting Deu 6:5.
“Love your enemies.”
“Simon … do you love me more than these? … You know that I love you.”

senses.definition: God's mercy, given as he wills; for the Hebrew piel of Exo 33:19 quoted.

evidence.note: Quoting Exo 33:19: “I will have mercy (אֵרַחֵמ) on whom I have mercy.”
“He has mercy on whom he will.”
“That he might have mercy on all.”

senses.definition: To be moved with pity and act on it: Jesus toward the crowds and the sick, the father toward his returning son; the cry “have mercy on us”.

evidence.note: Jesus saw the crowds “and had compassion on them, because they were weary and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd”.
“His father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell on his neck”, as Psa 103:13.
“Have mercy on us, son of David.”

senses.definition: To be loved; in Rom 9:25 for Hosea's “shown compassion”.

evidence.note: Quoting Hos 2:25: “her who was not beloved (אֵתֿרַחמַתֿ), beloved”.
“He who loves me will be loved (נֵתֿרחֵמ) by my Father.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܪܚܡܐ, nearly always plural ܪ̈ܚܡܐ, for σπλάγχνα, οἰκτιρμοί and ἔλεος, as the Hebrew רַחֲמִים.

senses.definition: God's compassion, and the tender affection of the inward parts that believers are to put on.

evidence.note: “Through the compassion (בּרַחמֵא) of the mercy of our God, by which the dayspring from on high will visit us.”
“The Father of mercies.”
“There were not even mercies upon you, but now mercies have been poured upon you”, from Hos 2:25.
“Withholds his compassion from him.”
“Blessed are the merciful, for on them will be mercy.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܪܚܡܢܐ, for οἰκτίρμων and ἐλεήμων.

senses.definition: Merciful, of the Father, of Jesus as high priest, and of those who are to be like the Father.

“The Lord is merciful and compassionate”, the words of Exo 34:6.

evidence.note: compassion, pity, commiseration; linked to Hebrew רָחַם.

doctrine.statement: When Moses asked to see Yahweh's glory, Yahweh answered, “I will proclaim the name of Yahweh before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will have compassion on whom I will have compassion” (Exo 33:19), and passing by he proclaimed, “Yahweh, Yahweh, a God compassionate (רַחוּם) and gracious, long of anger and abounding in covenant faithfulness and truth … forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, but who will by no means clear the guilty” (Exo 34:6–7). The words are repeated as the ground of hope: by Moses (Deu 4:31), by Hezekiah calling Israel to return (2Ch 30:9), in the psalms (Psa 86:15; 103:8; 145:8), in Joel's call to rend the heart (Jol 2:13), in Nehemiah's confession (Neh 9:17, 31), and in Jonah's complaint that the same compassion reached Nineveh (Jon 4:2). The adjective רַחוּם is used of God alone, and once of the upright who are like him (Psa 112:4). Paul quotes Exo 33:19 and concludes, “it is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy” (Rom 9:15–16), and James, “the Lord is very compassionate and merciful” (Jas 5:11). The wicked who forsakes his way will find it (Isa 55:7), and “he who confesses and forsakes his transgressions will be shown compassion” (Pro 28:13). From the verses: compassion is part of the name Yahweh declared of himself; it is his to give as he chooses, it is held out to all who turn to him, and it does not cancel his justice.

“As a father has compassion on his children, Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him. For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust. As for man, his days are like grass … the wind passes over it, and it is gone” (Psa 103:13–16). Of Israel in the wilderness: “he, being compassionate, covered iniquity and did not destroy them … for he remembered that they were flesh, a wind that goes and does not return” (Psa 78:38–39). Job asks why he did not die from the womb (Job 3:11; 10:18), and says of the wicked man that “the womb forgets him; the worm feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more” (Job 24:20). The same psalm that grounds compassion in man's dust praises Yahweh “who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with covenant faithfulness and compassion” (Psa 103:4). From the verses: Yahweh's compassion is grounded in what man is, dust and flesh, a breath that passes and does not return of itself; man has no life beyond death of his own, and his hope is Yahweh's compassion, which redeems life from the pit.

Moses foretold that after the curses and the scattering, “Yahweh your God will turn your captivity and have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where Yahweh your God has scattered you” (Deu 30:3). The prophets repeat it in the same words: “Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land” (Isa 14:1); “I will turn the captivity of the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings, and the city shall be built on its mound” (Jer 30:18); the seed of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob will have rulers from the seed of David, “for I will turn their captivity and have compassion on them” (Jer 33:26); “now I will turn the captivity of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel” (Ezk 39:25), after Gog and his northern armies fall on the mountains of Israel (Ezk 39:1–24); “I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion; my house shall be built in it” (Zec 1:16); “I will bring them back, for I have compassion on them” (Zec 10:6). Micah ends, “he will again have compassion on us … you will give truth to Jacob, covenant faithfulness to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers from days of old” (Mic 7:19–20), and Zechariah the priest blessed God, at the coming of Jesus, “to perform the mercy promised to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to Abraham” (Luk 1:72–73). From the verses: Yahweh's compassion on Israel is the keeping of his oath to Abraham, and it takes a literal form: the gathering of Israel from the nations to their own land, the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and a ruler of David's seed. The return from Babylon was a beginning; Ezekiel sets the full gathering after the northern invasion of Gog, and the oath to Abraham was still looked for when Jesus was born.

Hosea's daughter was named לֹא רֻחָמָה, “not shown compassion”, “for I will no more have compassion on the house of Israel”, while Judah would be shown compassion and saved “by Yahweh their God, and not by bow or sword” (Hos 1:6–7). The reversal is promised in the same chapter: “Say to your sisters, Ruhamah” (Hos 2:3), and “I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-ammi, You are my people, and he will say, My God” (Hos 2:25). Paul quotes the verse of those God has called “not from the Jews only, but also from the nations” (Rom 9:24–25), and Peter writes to believers, “who once were not a people, but now are the people of God; who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy” (1Pe 2:10). From the verses: compassion withdrawn for unfaithfulness is restored by Yahweh's own act and not earned; the apostles apply Hosea's promise to all whom God calls, Jew and Gentile, and the promise to Israel to be sown again in the land still stands.

Yahweh closes the womb and opens it (Gen 20:18; 29:31; 30:22; 1Sa 1:5–6), and he forms man in it (Job 31:15). Every firstborn “that opens the womb” is his, because he killed the firstborn of Egypt and spared Israel's: “therefore I sacrifice to Yahweh every male that opens the womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem” (Exo 13:2, 12–15; Num 3:12–13). Jeremiah was told, “before I formed you in the belly I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I set you apart” (Jer 1:5): Yahweh's foreknowledge and purpose for a man not yet formed. Luke records that Mary “bore her firstborn son”, and that he was brought to Jerusalem “as it is written in the law of the Lord, every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord” (Luk 2:7, 22–23). From the verses: life in the womb is Yahweh's work; Jesus came into being from his mother's womb as her firstborn, a man under the law of the firstborn, set apart to God from birth.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. BDB keys assigned: t.bz.ab רֶחֶם, t.bz.ac רַחֲמִים (the database files the same 45 plural tokens under both keys, so the counts overlap), t.bz.ad verb, t.bz.ae רַחוּם, t.bz.af רַחֲמָנִי, t.ca.ab and t.ca.ac רָחָם/רָחָמָה, xt.ah.ae Aramaic רַחֲמִין (root key רחמינ). Names in names/: jeroham (t.bz.aj, j.dk.ag), jerahmeel (t.bz.ak, t.bz.al gentilic), rehum (t.bz.ai, xt.ah.ad), raham (t.bz.ag, which also counts the Jdg 5:30 token), lo-ruhamah (l.ab.ad, t.bz.ah; lo.json leaves the name out). Stems: the brief's three no-stem tokens (Hos 1:6, 8; 2:25) are the name לֹא רֻחָמָה, a pual form; Hos 2:3 רֻחָמָה is tagged pual. Psa 18:2 is the only qal; 2Sa 22:2 lacks the line. Split: Arabic raḫam (vulture) shows ḫ against raḥim/raḥima (ḥ), so רָחָם is a second older root (rḫm) in the spelling; Lane's same article gives raḫama “affection, love” and the brooding hen, which may be a by-form or a loan of the rḥm sense; not decided. Open questions: (1) gender of רֶחֶם given mf on Jer 20:17 (feminine agreement) and Arabic raḥim (feminine); elsewhere no agreement decides it. (2) Is the qal “love” (Psa 18:2) a borrowing of the Aramaic sense? Only one verse; the Peshitta and Targums use the verb chiefly for love, Hebrew for compassion. (3) Ge'ez mḥr recorded as possible (metathesis); Dillmann column read from the OCR page header, check the scan. (4) σπλάγχνον is not a loan as the brief's “Greek loans” section suggests: Thayer only equates it with רַחֲמִים; recorded as a rendering, with the Peshitta's רַחְמָא for it in Luk 1:78, Php 1:8, 1Jn 3:17; the Septuagint alignment does not show it for רַחֲמִים (Pro 12:10 not aligned). (5) Syriac pointing of רְחֵם, רַחְמָא, מְרַחְמָנָא is mine from SEDRA's vocalised forms (root 1753 רחמ; lexemes 2997 verb, 2999 noun, 2994 adjective); Syriac stems assigned from the forms (etraḥḥam ethpaal “have compassion”, etrǝḥem ethpeel “be loved”). Left out of the Syriac: רָחְמָא “friend” (lexeme 2998, Jhn 15:13–15; Luk 11:5–8), רְחִימָא “beloved” (2996), רֵחְמְתָא “love, friendship” (3001), מְרַחְמָנוּתָא “compassion” (2995); they could be added. Leads not followed: Ugaritic rḥm “girl” and the goddess rḥmy (KTU 1.23), which would match Jdg 5:30 and the name Raham (DULAT not consulted); Old South Arabian rḥmn as a divine title (Biella, sabaweb); CAD R for rēmu and rêmu; Payne Smith for ܪܚܡ; Phoenician and Punic rḥm (Krahmalkov). Gen 43:30 and 1Ki 3:26 are not aligned in MACULA-LXX.
